title: Led by DeepSeek, Chinese AI models take top five positions in global weekly token usage ranking
source_used: Global Times (citing National Business Daily and OpenRouter data)
key_facts: Chinese AI models took the top five spots in weekly token usage on OpenRouter, a global large language model aggregation platform, for 5 to 11 Oct 2026.

Models worldwide processed 172 trillion tokens that week, up 3.61 percent; Chinese models accounted for 86.74 trillion tokens against 18.97 trillion for US models; Chinese usage grew 50.96 percent, US usage 17.1 percent (National Business Daily reported the figures on Monday).
It was the 24th consecutive week that Chinese models led US models in token usage.

DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash led with 41 trillion tokens (up 60 percent); Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash second with 12.2 trillion; Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Flash third with 11.5 trillion; StepFun's Step 5 Preview fourth with 8.84 trillion; Tencent's Hy4 preview fifth with 8.28 trillion.
Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 ranked eighth with 5.02 trillion tokens, up 104 percent week over week.
The five leading Chinese models accounted for 47.9 percent of tokens processed; it was not the first time Chinese models had taken all five top spots.

Tian Feng of the Fast Think Institute told Global Times the ranking endorses Chinese models' capabilities, stability and cost-effectiveness, noting DeepSeek raised API prices significantly in mid-August.
Chinese models accounted for just 6-13 percent of uses on OpenRouter in February, according to CNBC as cited by Global Times.
quote_evidence: Chinese AI models have taken the top five spots in weekly token usage, according to the latest data from OpenRouter, a global large language model (LLM) aggregation platform.
This marked the 24th consecutive week that Chinese models led their US counterparts in token usage.
A token is the basic unit of text processed by an AI model and it has become a key measure of AI usage and computing consumption.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheap, openly available Chinese models are winning large developer usage on one major marketplace, which bears on which models developers build on.
event_date: Week of 5 to 11 Oct 2026; Global Times article 12 Oct 2026.
